schema: One entry per table that holds a visitor datum (IP, user agent, browser device id, possessed session token, accessor e-mail). identityColumns: the columns that carry it. producers: every insertInto site as `file :: function`. readers: the functions that read the datum back (`file :: function`). cleanup: { job, functions } (functions as `file :: function`, exported by that file and called by the job) or { exception: reason }. erase: { routes, functions } or { exception: reason }. tests: files that pin the lifetime or the exception and name the table. reference: the heading anchor in docs/reference/analytics-privacy.md. Checked against the source tree by tests/anonymous-visitor-stores-gate.test.js (B786).

slide_views.note: No identity column of its own: a row belongs to a view_sessions row through view_session_id and shares its lifetime and erasure.

erase.exception: IP-only deduplication record without an identifier a visitor could present to prove it is theirs; it expires within ACCESS_ATTEMPT_WINDOW_MS (24 hours) plus one job interval regardless (GDPR art. 11, B785).

user_notifications.note: No visitor datum since B785: the access_attempt notification names the deck and the access type, and migration 093 stripped accessorIp from older rows. Listed so a second insert site fails rule (b); createNotification receives data opaquely, so the absence of accessorIp in the JSON is pinned by tests/access-attempt-retention.test.js, not by this gate.

cleanup.exception: The recipient's own inbox data, holding nothing of the visitor; it falls under inbox controls (read, archive) and cascades away with the deck or organization. There is no age cleanup of notifications (out of scope of the privacy work, B786 brief § Buiten scope).

erase.exception: Nothing of the visitor remains in the row to erase (B785); tests/access-attempt-retention.test.js pins the absence of accessorIp.

share_link_guests.note: Share-link guest: an e-mail-verified person invited to or verified on one share link, not an anonymous visitor. The insert writes the e-mail; the possessed session token arrives through updateTable().set() in verifyGuestEmail, so this line exists since the gate reads .set() as well (B811).

cleanup.exception: The row is the guest's access grant to one share link and lives as long as the link (share_link_id → presentation_share_links ON DELETE CASCADE) or until the author removes the guest. The session token stops resolving at session_expires_at, seven days after verification, and on a revoked or expired link, checked on every read by getGuestBySessionToken; it is not cleared from the row, and there is no age cleanup.

feedback.note: Audience member of a live session: a browser-generated device id keyed to the session, so one entry per device. Not a visitor of a share link; registered because the id is the same kind of identifier analytics protects.

erase.exception: The row lives and dies with its 24-hour live session (feedback.session_id → present_sessions ON DELETE CASCADE, collected by the live-session sweep) and the presenter can clear the slide with resetFeedback; the device id is browser-generated and proves nothing about whose it is (GDPR art. 11, same reasoning as the analytics device id), so there is no visitor erase route.

interaction_votes.note: Audience member of a live session: one vote per device per poll or likert interaction, keyed by a browser-generated device id.

erase.exception: The row lives and dies with its 24-hour live session (interaction_votes.interaction_id → interactions → present_sessions ON DELETE CASCADE, collected by the live-session sweep) and the presenter can clear the poll with resetPollInteraction / resetLikertInteraction; the device id is browser-generated and proves nothing about whose it is (GDPR art. 11), so there is no visitor erase route.

magic_link_tokens.note: Account token, not an anonymous visitor: the IP and user agent of the request that asked for a sign-in link for a known address.

password_reset_tokens.note: Account token, not an anonymous visitor: the IP and user agent of the request that asked for a reset link; invitation tokens written by users.js carry neither.

auth_audit_log.note: Authentication audit: the IP and user agent of sign-in, reset and magic-link events, with the address they were attempted for. Security record of the instance, kept 90 days.

erase.exception: An instance security record: a failed sign-in for an address has to stay visible to the operator for the 90-day window whoever asks, and the row has no organization column to bind a request to (storage-scope.md category 5). It ages out through cleanupOldAuditLogs.
